en.title: ai
en.summary: This is the letter L319 from the vowel-consonant groups.

sections.title: The letters ai
paragraphs: The letters ai make three different sounds. You hear their main sound in the word (rain) /reɪn/, which means water that falls from clouds. The letters say their name like the vowel in (wait) /weɪt/. Look at each word closely to choose the right sound.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, open your mouth slightly and slide your tongue forward and up. For the second sound, keep your tongue mid and front, letting air flow freely. For the third sound, relax your tongue in the central part of your mouth. A schwa is a short, weak vowel in the middle of the mouth. Touch your throat to feel each vowel make it shake.

sections.title: Reading the letters
paragraphs: In most stressed syllables, these letters sound like (rain) /reɪn/. Before certain letters, they sound open like (said) /sɛd/ or (air) /ɛər/. In an unstressed syllable, they sound short and weak like (captain) /kæp.tən/ or (curtain) /kɜːr.tən/.

sections.title: Sounds to avoid
paragraphs: Do not read these letters as two separate sounds. Say them as one smooth movement. When you see (wait) /weɪt/, do not shorten the sound into the flat vowel of (said) /sɛd/. In weak endings like (curtain) /kɜːr.tən/, do not use the strong vowel of (rain) /reɪn/. Keep your voice relaxed on the weak parts.
